title: Your kidneys filter 180 litres a day but you pee only a litre or two
body: Each adult kidney contains around a million nephrons, microscopic filtering units, and together the two kidneys receive roughly **20 to 25% of the heart’s output**. From that blood they generate about 180 litres of filtrate a day: water, salts, glucose and waste all pass through. The nephron’s long tubule then reclaims almost everything useful and returns it to the blood. What is left, normally 800 to 2,000 millilitres a day, is urine. Filtering nearly everything and taking back only what is needed lets the body fine-tune its water and salt balance.

slides.question: What happens to most of the 180 litres your kidneys filter each day?
options: It is stored in the bladder
It is reabsorbed into the blood
It is broken down by the liver
slides.explanation: Most of the filtrate is reabsorbed along the nephron’s tubule. Only about 800 to 2,000 mL a day ends up as urine.

slides.alt: Animation: two glass tanks on one scale hold a day's 180 litres of filtrate and 0.8 to 2 litres of urine; 120 bottles of 1.5 litres fill; a simplified nephron diagram shows filtering and reabsorption; all but about one bottle drains back, leaving the urine.

slides.label: of filtrate your kidneys produce in a day
slides.text: About 99% is reabsorbed. The 800 to 2,000 mL that remain leave as urine.

slides.heading: Of every 100 litres your kidneys filter, about 99 go back into the blood
slides.note: About 180 litres of filtrate a day; only 0.8 to 2 litres leave as urine

slides.heading: Inside a nephron
items: Blood arrives: the kidneys take 20 to 25% of the heart’s output
A tuft of capillaries, the glomerulus, filters out water and small molecules
The tubule reabsorbs the water, salts and glucose the body needs
What is left drains to the bladder as urine

slides.heading: A million filters
slides.text: Each adult human kidney holds around one million nephrons; a mouse kidney has only about 12,500. The whole organ is only about 12 centimetres long, which makes the daily 180 litres all the more remarkable.

slides.clue: The kidney’s microscopic filtering unit; each adult kidney holds around a million of them
slides.detail: From the Greek nephros, ‘kidney’. A tuft of capillaries filters the blood, and a long tubule takes back what the body needs.
